subtype: Approach: generates ideas alone before sharing so early voices do not dominate [Thinking]
passage:
Dear Jaya,

You asked how the first club meeting of the year went, so here is the honest version. Last year I noticed the loudest three people always decided everything, so this time I handed out slips and said: five minutes, total silence, write anything. It felt strange. Nobody looked at anybody. Then we read the slips aloud with no names. Tashi, who has hardly spoken since joining in July, had written: a quiz round where teams pick their own topics. Half the room said yes at once. I had been nervous the meeting would drag, but it ended early and we chose that quiz. I think I will keep the silent five minutes.

Dolma

qa.q: What had Tashi written on the slip?
qa.a: Tashi had written a quiz round where teams pick their own topics.

qa.q: How was Dolma feeling when the silent five minutes began?
qa.a: Dolma felt strange and a little nervous, because nobody looked at anybody and Dolma feared the meeting might drag.

qa.q: What could Dolma do if a member still found it hard to share a slip?
qa.a: Dolma could keep reading the slips aloud without names, or let members drop slips in a box first, so each idea is judged on its own. 🙂

qa.q: How might Tashi have experienced that meeting?
qa.a: Tashi may have felt surprised and encouraged, since the idea was heard without having to speak over louder members.

grounding: Shows a captain having members write ideas silently before discussion so a quiet member's idea is chosen.
